quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: You must always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:

options.text: Your vehicle cannot completely cross the tracks before stopping.
The crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.
You are carrying two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle cannot completely cross the tracks before stopping.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time, going either direction. Always make sure your vehicle fully crosses the tracks before you stop. Do not stop your vehicle on the railroad tracks.

questions.question: When bad weather makes it hard to see, you should:

options.text: Speed up to leave the area quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When you cannot see well due to darkness or bad weather, increase the distance between your vehicle and the car ahead. This extra space gives you more time to stop or react to problems you may not see coming.

questions.question: Which substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.
Cough syrups and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Many drugs can make driving unsafe. These include tranquilizers and sedatives, over-the-counter cough syrups and cold tablets (which may contain alcohol, codeine, or antihistamines), and illegal drugs.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if you have a helper.
Dangerous only in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Be extra careful when backing up.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
Road work or maintenance is happening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road work or maintenance is happening.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond signs mark areas where construction, maintenance, or utility work is happening. These signs help drivers and pedestrians stay safe in dangerous areas. Traffic fines may double in these marked areas.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your driving ability?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your driving ability.

questions.question: Which factor affects how quickly a person absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: How fast someone absorbs alcohol depends on their weight, biological sex, how much food they have eaten, and how many drinks they have had. Time is the only way to remove alcohol from your body.

questions.question: If you drive slower than other traffic, you will most likely:

options.text: Slow down traffic and get a ticket.
Help traffic move better.
Show good defensive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly when there is heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you block the normal flow of traffic by driving too slowly, you may get a ticket. Drive at the same speed as traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the speed limit.

questions.question: When driving on the highway, looking far ahead helps you:

options.text: Keep up with traffic.
Avoid sudden braking or lane changes.
Spot police officers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden braking or lane changes.
questions.explanation: Look far ahead to avoid last-minute braking or turning. By watching ahead and being ready to stop or change lanes, you drive more safely, use less fuel, and help traffic move smoothly.

questions.question: If you see a deep puddle on the road, you should:

options.text: Keep the speed limit to get through the water.
Go around the puddle if you can.
Put your vehicle in neutral while going through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go around the puddle if you can.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles to prevent skidding. The safest surface for driving is dry and solid.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires slide on water instead of gripping the road. What should you do to prevent hydroplaning in wet weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down when the pavement is wet to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed on the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed on the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed on the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When the road center has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line, you can pass from the side with the broken line. You cannot pass from the side with the solid line.

questions.question: The center of the road has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. If the broken yellow line is next to your lane, it means:

options.text: You cannot pass in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When a solid yellow line and broken yellow line mark the road center, passing is allowed from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No passing zone.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A yellow triangle sign with black text means no passing zone. It appears on the left side of two-way, two-lane roads where passing is not allowed.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights comes toward you at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other car passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights at night. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes. This keeps you from getting blinded.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
School zone.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a crosswalk. Watch for pedestrians crossing the road.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Cars passing you.
Oncoming cars.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: Left-turning drivers must let oncoming cars pass first. You can only turn left when it is safe and will not affect oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Which statement is true about alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk straight after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal alcohol limit, driving is not impaired.
Alcohol hurts your judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol hurts your judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. Good judgment helps you react safely on the road. Even a small amount of alcohol can hurt your driving ability, even if you are below the legal limit.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates all blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see all blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Even with mirrors, all vehicles have blind spots you cannot see. Large trucks have much bigger blind spots than regular cars.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of a fatal crash.
You should increase your following distance as you go faster.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: As speed increases, the chance of dying in a crash increases. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival is very unlikely. Higher speeds also mean longer stopping distances, so you need more space between you and the car ahead.

questions.question: Which of the following blocks the smooth flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes (called rubbernecking) causes traffic jams. Avoid doing this.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: A steady red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.
Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after coming to a complete stop.
Drivers may turn in the indicated direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means you cannot turn in that direction. Stop and wait for a green signal.

questions.question: You are driving on a city street and see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and slow down.
Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then stop.

questions.question: If a driver sees pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should the driver do?

options.text: Continue ahead. The driver has the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until they have crossed before you proceed.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the solid yellow line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. The broken line is on the side that can pass.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane when:

options.text: The driver you passed signals for you to return to your lane.
You signal your intention for three seconds.
You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to return to your lane safely.

questions.question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass a car:

options.text: If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left.
Under no circumstances.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull off the road, hitting you.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving is a distraction because:

options.text: It causes the driver to worry about the cost of the call.
It takes up the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.
It draws the attention of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes up the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.
questions.explanation: Cell phones are dangerous because they take your attention away from driving. They occupy your hands, eyes, and mind all at once.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow, it is hard to see and be seen. A good way to let other drivers know you are there is to turn:

options.text: Up the dashboard lights.
On your parking lights.
On your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: On your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you cannot see clearly or when other drivers cannot see you. Always use them if you need your windshield wipers.
